zh: 归根结底，有一个问题：好吧，折旧寿命大约是六年。

speaker: Unknown
en: So once they're fully depreciated and given the power efficiency of newer generations, et cetera, it does make sense to replace them and upgrade them.
zh: 所以一旦它们完全折旧，考虑到新一代的电源效率等等，更换和升级它们确实是合理的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not that we do replace the chips, but it's really the systems.
zh: 并不是说我们更换芯片，而是更换整个系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in other words, we think in terms of pods.
zh: 换句话说，我们以 pod 为单位来思考。

speaker: Unknown
en: So a TPU, let's say, AT pod might be 9,600 chips.
zh: 比如一个 TPU，一个 pod 可能有 9,600 个芯片。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it might be 140 something, 152 racks, et cetera.
zh: 而且可能是 140 多个、152 个机架等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: So then we would say, okay, we're going to pull out that pod and we're going to replace it with a, whatever it is, TPU 12 or 13 or 14 pod.
zh: 然后我们会说，好吧，我们要把那个 pod 拔出来，用一个——不管是什么——TPU 12 或 13 或 14 的 pod 来替换它。

speaker: Unknown
en: It might not be a perfect fit, which then we have to, in other words, the new pods footprint might not be a perfect fit for the old pods vacancy.
zh: 它可能不是完美契合，换句话说，新 pod 的占地空间可能和旧 pod 腾出的位置不完全匹配。

speaker: Unknown
en: We then just have to account for that.
zh: 那我们只需要把这一点考虑进去。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have to figure out how we would retrofit.
zh: 我们必须想清楚如何进行改造升级。

speaker: Unknown
en: We can't plan that because we don't know what that many generations of TPUs are going to be.
zh: 我们没法规划这个，因为我们不知道这么多代 TPU 会是什么样子。

speaker: Unknown
en: So then it's, again, a bit of an art to figure out how we would, and it's actually hard work, figure out how we would decom and then replace as quickly as possible with new TPUs.
zh: 所以这就又有点像一门艺术，去想清楚我们该怎么——而且这确实是艰苦的工作——想清楚我们如何拆解，然后尽快用新 TPU 替换。

speaker: Unknown
en: You've written publicly about open standards.
zh: 你曾公开撰文谈过开放标准。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you say a word on that?
zh: 能就此说几句吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so I think that we talked about this interoperability question.
zh: 好，我想我们谈过这个互操作性的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so for us, while we support vertical integration and we make it possible to extract just as much performance as you want, for us, it's really important to not force lock-in and not force a sort of walled garden in terms of how the system works end to end.
zh: 对我们来说，虽然我们支持垂直整合，并且让你能够按需提取尽可能多的性能，但对我们来说，非常重要的是不强制锁定，不强制某种围墙花园，不论是在系统端到端的运作方式上。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, I'll give one example.
zh: 那么，我举一个例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: At Google, we've developed a model development framework called JAX.
zh: 在 Google，我们开发了一个叫 JAX 的模型开发框架。

speaker: Unknown
en: We like it a lot.
zh: 我们非常喜欢它。

speaker: Unknown
en: We think it's really, really good.
zh: 我们认为它非常非常好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we use it extensively internally.
zh: 我们在内部大量使用它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Many of our customers like PyTorch.
zh: 我们的许多客户喜欢 PyTorch。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so one thing we could say is, hey, if you want to run on TPUs, you got to use JAX.
zh: 所以我们本可以说：嘿，如果你想在 TPU 上运行，你就得用 JAX。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's the best.
zh: 它是最好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm being facetious a little bit, but maybe it is, maybe it isn't.
zh: 我有点在开玩笑，但也许它是，也许不是。

speaker: Unknown
en: We think it's the best.
zh: 我们认为它是最好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's your only choice because it's so great.
zh: 而且那是你唯一的选择，因为它太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or we could say, look, if you like JAX, we like JAX.
zh: 或者我们可以说：看，如果你喜欢 JAX，我们也喜欢 JAX。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you like JAX, you can use it.
zh: 如果你喜欢 JAX，你可以用它。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you like PyTorch, we have Torch TPU, where your unmodified models, et cetera, can run.
zh: 但如果你喜欢 PyTorch，我们有 Torch TPU，你未修改的模型等等都可以在上面运行。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've seen this throughout history, actually, with many, many examples.
zh: 其实在历史上，我们已经见过很多很多这样的例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've used the example of IP.
zh: 我用过 IP 的例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why did the internet protocol win?
zh: 为什么互联网协议赢了？

speaker: Unknown
en: There were actually many competing protocols to IP.
zh: 实际上曾有许多与 IP 竞争的协议。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is ancient history in the 70s and early 80s.
zh: 这是很久以前的事了，在 70 年代和 80 年代初。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why did IP win?
zh: 为什么 IP 赢了？

speaker: Unknown
en: It was because it was open standard and it was this narrow waist to the hourglass where anything could run on top in terms of software and anything could run underneath it in terms of hardware.
zh: 那是因为它是开放标准，它是沙漏的那个细腰，任何软件都可以在上面运行，任何硬件都可以在其下运行。

speaker: Unknown
en: So open standard, interoperable, anyone who brought IP could plug into a router port and become part of the internet.
zh: 所以开放标准、可互操作，任何持有 IP 的人都可以插到路由器端口上，成为互联网的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was beautiful.
zh: 那非常美妙。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's what allowed the internet to explode in its growth and reach across the world.
zh: 而这正是让互联网能够爆发式增长、覆盖全世界的原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we really do believe in those open standards in terms of plugin points.
zh: 所以我们真的相信那些开放标准，在插件接入点方面。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, if you want to plug in something highly specialized,
zh: 现在，如果你想接入一些高度定制化的东西，

speaker: Unknown
en: You can.
zh: 你可以。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you think that you've got a better thing to plug into our framework, you absolutely can.
zh: 如果你认为你有一个更好的东西可以接入我们的框架，你完全可以。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we want to really support open standards, ideally open source around it as well.
zh: 但我们想要真正支持开放标准，理想情况下还有围绕它的开源。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's too big and too important to build out to be any one vendor's closed proprietary stack.
zh: 这件事太庞大、太重要，不能建成任何一家厂商的封闭专有技术栈。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We really believe that.
zh: 我们真的这么认为。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's got to be one of choice.
zh: 而且它必须是自由选择的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's also why, for example, we fully support and have TPUs, GPUs, other accelerators, et cetera.
zh: 这也是为什么，比如说，我们全面支持并且拥有 TPU、GPU、其他加速器等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: How has day-to-day life for your team changed with AI?
zh: AI 如何改变了你团队的日常？

speaker: Unknown
en: Where is it changing your function the most?
zh: 它在哪些地方最大程度地改变了你的职能？

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think whatever you want to say, the easiest answer is on the software engineering side, where it's been documented externally quite a bit.
zh: 我想不管你怎么说，最简单的答案是在软件工程方面，这方面在外部已经被记录得相当多了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think that we are, at Google and my team, using it to great effect in terms of our software development capabilities, but also, frankly, tests, rollouts, even helping with design, et cetera.
zh: 所以我认为，在 Google 和我的团队里，我们在软件开发能力方面用它用得很有成效，但坦率地说，还有测试、发布，甚至在设计方面的辅助等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: But there have been, on the hardware side, which has maybe gotten less external coverage, also significant change.
zh: 但在硬件方面——这方面得到的外部报道可能较少——也发生了重大变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: In other words, my hardware engineers, I was just looking at the numbers earlier today, in fact, are using AI, using whatever, the token counts, if you want, not the best metric, but it's still a metric.
zh: 换句话说，我的硬件工程师——其实我今天早些时候刚看了数据——正在使用 AI，使用 whatever，token 数量吧，如果你愿意的话，这不是最好的指标，但它仍然是一个指标。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our hardware engineers are using AI as much as the software engineers are.
zh: 我们的硬件工程师使用 AI 的程度和软件工程师一样多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And productivity has gone up.
zh: 而且生产力已经提升了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Time from design kickoff to tape out is shrinking.
zh: 从设计启动到流片的时间在缩短。

speaker: Unknown
en: Time for bring up is shrinking.
zh: 调试上线(bring up)的时间在缩短。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in other words, productivity is going up significantly.
zh: 也就是说，生产力在显著提升。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then other maybe less expected changes, how we do data center design.
zh: 但还有一些可能不那么意料之中的变化，比如我们如何做数据中心设计。

speaker: Unknown
en: has changed significantly.
zh: 已经发生了显著变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: In other words, how we evaluate, you mentioned, hey, do we do a gigawatt building or 100 megawatt campus or 200 megawatt campus?
zh: 换句话说，我们如何评估，你提到过，嘿，我们是做吉瓦级的大楼，还是 100 兆瓦的园区，还是 200 兆瓦的园区？

speaker: Unknown
en: In the past, this would be very detailed, very sort of spreadsheet-driven, human-driven processes.
zh: 在过去，这是非常详细的、非常由电子表格驱动的、人工驱动的流程。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it still is to some extent, but there's a lot of AI now involved that really streamlines the process in terms of planning and development as well.
zh: 现在在一定程度上仍然如此，但现在有大量 AI 参与其中，在规划和开发方面大大简化了这个流程。

speaker: Unknown
en: Interesting.
zh: 有意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's like reasoning models?
zh: 是像推理模型那样的东西吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I wouldn't say quite yet reasoning models.
zh: 我还不能说已经是推理模型了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not replacing human judgment, but it's making it much easier to bring the necessary information together in one place and basically put the right information in front of the humans making the decisions.
zh: 它并没有取代人类的判断，但它让把必要的信息汇集到一个地方、基本上把正确的信息摆在做决策的人面前变得容易得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: OK, I'm going to bring us home with two kind of out there, kind of fun questions.
zh: 好的，我要用两个比较天马行空、比较有趣的问题来收尾。

speaker: Unknown
en: Question number one, orbital data centers.
zh: 第一个问题，轨道数据中心。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've seen that Google is thinking about this quite seriously, and you don't need to comment on that.
zh: 我看到 Google 正在相当认真地思考这个问题，你不需要对此发表评论。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I mean, does the fact that people are seriously running the numbers on orbital computes mean that there are kind of serious binding constraints on Earth?
zh: 但我的意思是，人们在认真计算轨道计算的账，这是否意味着地球上存在某种真正硬性的约束条件？

speaker: Unknown
en: And what do you think of orbital data centers?
zh: 你怎么看轨道数据中心？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, it's an exciting direction.
zh: 是的，这是一个令人兴奋的方向。

speaker: Unknown
en: We are actually pursuing it, and we've referred to it more with no tongue-in-cheek as a moonshot, as one of our big efforts that we're excited about investing in.
zh: 我们实际上正在推进它，我们更多是认真地——不是开玩笑地——称之为一个 moonshot(登月计划)，是我们兴奋投入的重大努力之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: It goes back to the earlier part of the conversation where you raised, I think correctly, that in terms of fundamental constraints, energy and energy production is a key, key challenge.
zh: 这回到对话的前面部分，你提出的，我认为提得很对，就是在根本性约束方面，能源和能源生产是一个关键的关键挑战。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so really, bottom line is, from a fundamentals perspective,
zh: 所以，真正的底线是，从基本原理的角度来看，

speaker: Unknown
en: In space, you have something like 40% more power available because of lack of attenuation in the atmosphere, et cetera.
zh: 在太空中，由于没有大气衰减等等，你大约有 40% 更多的可用功率。

speaker: Unknown
en: In other words, it's just more solar capacity, 1.4x.
zh: 换句话说，就是更多的太阳能容量，1.4 倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's one part of it.
zh: 这是其中一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: But in a sun-synchronous orbit, you have 90 to 100% coverage of sunlight on your solar cells relative to 28, 30, maybe 35%.
zh: 但在太阳同步轨道上，你的太阳能电池有 90 到 100% 的光照覆盖率，而地面上只有 28%、30%，也许 35%。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in other words, just this enormous amount of power, obviously the sun, you take the 1.4x and you take the 3 to 4x in terms of number of hours per day, you remove batteries more or less from the equation.
zh: 换句话说，仅仅是这么巨大的功率，显然是太阳，你把 1.4 倍乘上每天 3 到 4 倍的小时数，再把电池差不多从等式中去掉。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now you have the potential for something that can really, and of course carbon-free, lots of benefits, lots of challenges.
zh: 现在你就有了一种真正……的潜力，当然还有无碳，很多好处，也很多挑战。

speaker: Unknown
en: Lots and lots of challenges.
zh: 非常非常多的挑战。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in other words, okay, now what about cooling?
zh: 换句话说，好，那散热呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: Naively you might think cooling in space is easier, it's actually harder.
zh: 直觉上你可能觉得太空中的散热更容易，实际上更难。

speaker: Unknown
en: Reliability.
zh: 可靠性。

speaker: Unknown
en: We talked about how these things fail sometimes.
zh: 我们谈过这些东西有时会出故障。

speaker: Unknown
en: Repairs becomes harder.
zh: 维修变得更难。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not impossible, but it becomes harder in space.
zh: 不是不可能，但在太空中变得更难了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Networking.
zh: 网络。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can pull the robot up with the cluster.
zh: 你可以带着集群把机器人拉上去。

speaker: Unknown
en: Exactly.
zh: 没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: So perhaps there'll be that this model is a promising direction.
zh: 所以也许这种模式会是一个有前景的方向。

speaker: Unknown
en: Redundancy will probably be your friend.
zh: 冗余很可能会是你的朋友。

speaker: Unknown
en: Your prescient question on free space optics is now going to become reality.
zh: 你那个关于自由空间光通信的很有预见性的问题，现在将要变成现实。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're probably not going to be stringing fiber between these components, so it will actually be free space, and we're going to have the lasers pointing at the receivers and calibrating in real time.
zh: 我们大概不会在这些组件之间拉光纤，所以它真的会是自由空间，我们会让激光器对着接收器并实时校准。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are no showstoppers here, no fundamental showstoppers.
zh: 这里没有什么致命障碍，没有根本性的致命障碍。

speaker: Unknown
en: Last question.
zh: 最后一个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've had this image of the ineffable big supercomputer that you built them in my head this whole time.
zh: 这段时间以来，我脑子里一直有你建造的那台难以言喻的巨型超级计算机的画面。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so here's the question.
zh: 所以问题是这样的。

speaker: Unknown
en: 10 years from now, what will the most frontier supercomputer look like?
zh: 10 年后，最前沿的超级计算机会是什么样子？

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh my gosh, yeah, so 10 years is right at that edge where it's, I would say, in all sincerity, probably some people are thinking about what the 2036 computer looks like.
zh: 哦天哪，是的，10 年正好处于那个边缘，说实话，可能已经有人在思考 2036 年的计算机会是什么样子了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We might have a few thinking that far ahead, but wow, the cone of uncertainty there is way, way too wide.
zh: 我们也许有少数几个人在想那么远的事，但哇，那里的不确定性锥体实在是太、太宽了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like in those, if you look at the trends,
zh: 就像，如果你看那些趋势，

speaker: Unknown
en: The level of integration is going to be tremendous.
zh: 集成的程度将会是非常惊人的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, you know, we saw the beautiful fiber and the VR200 racks that we put together for Ineffable.
zh: 所以，你知道，我们看到了为 Ineffable 组装的那些漂亮的光纤和 VR200 机架。

speaker: Unknown
en: My guess is it's going to be more integrated, less fiber to, I won't say no fiber in 2036, but I think that probably from a rack perspective,
zh: 我的猜测是，它会更加集成化，光纤更少，我不敢说 2036 年会完全没有光纤，但我认为从机架的角度来看，

speaker: Unknown
en: The rack will look much more tightly integrated, and the amount of fiber, there'll be maybe a small fiber bundle coming out of the rack.
zh: 机架会看起来集成得更紧密，光纤的数量，可能只有一小束光纤从机架里引出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then, so in other words, one view you might have from a modular manufacturing perspective is these racks, likely in 2036, are gonna be manufactured centrally.
zh: 换句话说，从模块化制造的角度，你可能会有这样一种看法：这些机架，在 2036 年很可能会是集中化制造的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so whether they have 72, or 144, or 288, or probably more, 576, 1152, pick your favorite multiple of GPUs, since we're talking about the ineffable case, but then be the same for the TPUs, deeply integrated into a rack, would a rack be multiple megawatts?
zh: 所以不管它们是 72，还是 144，还是 288，或者可能更多，576，1152，随你挑一个喜欢的 GPU 倍数——既然我们说的是 ineffable 的情况——但 TPU 也一样，深度集成进一个机架，一个机架会不会达到数兆瓦？

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't know exactly how, but 2036, we get to imagine things, could be multiple megawatts in a single rack.
zh: 我们不完全清楚会怎样，但 2036 年，我们可以尽情想象，单个机架里可能是数兆瓦。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now you bring water, and you bring power, and you bring fiber, right?
zh: 到那时你接上水，接上电，接上光纤，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: You wheel that rack in, you plug those three things in, and you're off to the races as well.
zh: 你把那个机架推进来，把这三样东西插上，你就可以开工了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, so it's not gonna be like a big alien orb then?
zh: 好吧，所以它不会是一个巨大的外星人球体那样的东西？

speaker: Unknown
en: Up in space.
zh: 在太空里。

speaker: Unknown
en: By 2036, I wouldn't say that it's not possible for 2036 for it to be then directly launched into space and then maybe taken by a robotic arm at some space station and then plugged into the right module.
zh: 到 2036 年，我不能说这不可能：到 2036 年，它直接发射到太空，然后也许被某个空间站的机械臂接住，再插进正确的模块。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe that for 2036.
zh: 也许 2036 年会是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Fun.
zh: 有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: Fun to think about.
zh: 想想就很有意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: I really enjoyed this conversation.
zh: 我非常享受这次对话。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is the most intense, biggest CapEx build-out in history, but I also think it's a technology revolution that is a thing of beauty.
zh: 这是史上最激烈、规模最大的资本支出建设，但我也认为这是一场技术革命，是一件美的事物。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think
zh: 而且我认为

speaker: Unknown
en: You have such a grasp over the beauty of the technology and the binding constraints and how to balance this all.
zh: 你对这门技术之美、那些 binding constraints 以及如何平衡这一切，有着如此深刻的把握。

speaker: Unknown
en: Google is in good hands.
zh: Google 交到了好人手里。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you for taking the time to share what you're doing.
zh: 感谢你抽出时间分享你正在做的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a ton of fun.
zh: 这非常有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: We get to live through this and we get to define it.
zh: 我们能亲身经历这一切，而且我们能去定义它。

speaker: Unknown
en: So thank you very much.
zh: 所以非常感谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a great conversation.
zh: 这是一次很棒的对话。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you.
zh: 谢谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks.
zh: 谢谢。
